title: MIND: multimodal integration with neighbourhood-aware distributions
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74413-1

Multi-omics data integration is challenging due to missingness and inherent heterogeneity, current methods rely on assumptions that can cause information distortion. Here, the authors propose MIND, a platform that learns patient-specific embeddings from incomplete datasets.

title: Ionic self-assembled monolayers enable neutral interfaces and synergistic charge extraction in high-efficiency perovskite solar cells
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74288-2

Self-assembled monolayers are common hole-selective contacts in inverted perovskite solar cells, but acidic head groups reduce interface quality. Yang et al. neutralize these groups with alkali metal phosphonate salts and mixed layers, improving charge extraction, stability, and efficiency.

title: RGS22 is a metazoa-specific radial spoke component required for coordinated ciliary beating
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74801-7

Here they show that RGS22 is a metazoa-specific component of the cilia radial spoke. Knockout of Rgs22 in mice causes ciliary ultrastructural defects, impaired tissue-level coordination, and postnatal hydrocephalus.

title: Spatiotemporal flux breathing and topological sculpting in structured transverse orbital angular momentum lattices
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74644-2

This study shows how ultrafast optical vortices can be shaped into programmable space-time lattices, creating new ways to control light flow and encode information for high-dimensional optical communication.

title: Divergent responses of soil organic and inorganic carbon driven by land use during coastal reclamation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74876-2

Coastal reclamation drives divergent soil organic and inorganic carbon dynamics, with organic carbon becoming increasingly stable while inorganic carbon depletes under long-term terrestrial land use.

title: National pathways of land-use CO₂ emissions in the 21<sup>st</sup> century
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74836-w

The authors use a compact Earth system model OSCAR across SSP and idealized scenarios to show that policy timing and ambition are the primary determinants of whether the land sector becomes a durable carbon sink or remains a persistent source.

title: Pseudouridine synthase PUS1 and initiation factor mtIF2 are human mitoribosomal small subunit assembly factors
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 24 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74700-x

Cellular energy production depends on mitochondrial translation. Here, using cryoEM, the authors describe 12 assembly states of the human mitoribosomal small subunit and identify PUS1 and mtIF2 as mitoribosome assembly factors.
